Distillery 'often favours different sherry maturations'.
Official infobox states "Citrus notes" as a taste characteristic.
Reviews consistently describe a sherried nose (sherry, cola, apples).
Palate described as malty/creamy with vanilla sweetness.
Producer describes the core Lowland style as 'light, fruity and elegant'.
Described as a sweet, fruity malt.
Artificial cinnamon (Atomic Fireball candy) flavouring defines every bottling, not a natural cask characteristic.

Infobox lists cask_1 = 'American oak' for the core range; read as conventional ex-bourbon barrels, standard for Speyside, but the infobox does not use the word bourbon explicitly, hence low confidence.
Wikipedia: relaunched 2017 as known for its fruity single malt expressions.
Core range matured in ex-oloroso/PX sherry casks per Wikipedia; not universal (e.g. the Peated NAS uses Oloroso too, but other cask types exist), hence baseline not require.
Wikipedia: produces a traditional Highland malt with a heavy sherry influence.
Citrus blossom and green apple notes cited alongside honey.
Classic Glenlivet profile: pear, apple, honey, citrus blossom, vanilla.
Vanilla noted alongside honey and citrus.
Everything matures in sherry-seasoned oak sourced from Jerez.
Vanilla notes recur across multiple official variant descriptions (Rum Cask Finish, Sherry Cask Finish).
Whole range matured in sherry casks (American/European oak) from Oloroso producers per the distillery's own Wikipedia profile -- a genuine house-style signature, not a per-bottling variation.
Smoke is tea-maceration-derived (proprietary Asian tea blend), explicitly NOT peat -- analogous to Jack Daniel's charcoal mellowing.
Same source describes a floral character alongside fruitiness.
House style described as fruity, floral, subtly spicy from unpeated malt.
Infobox: 'Kilbeggan Blend ... Fresh Bourbon Casks, small portion in 2nd and 3rd'.
Historically matured only in sherry-seasoned oak from Jerez; today's range (Triple Cask/Double Cask) also uses bourbon casks, so "baseline" rather than "require".
First-fill Oloroso sherry-cask extra-maturation for at least six months is the defining production step.

Every drop exclusively aged in Oloroso sherry-seasoned oak per the distillery's own account -- sherry-only maturation, no bourbon-cask expressions in the core range.
House style built explicitly around honeyed character; product name references it directly.
Rye-forward mash; launch press release positions it explicitly as 'bolder, spicier'.

Matured partly in sherry butts (alongside Malaga wine casks and bourbon barrels) per company records.
